Deposit paid at booking

sampleInvoice.notes: Balance due at time of service. The deposit is non-refundable and applied to the total. Touch-up must be completed within 8 weeks of the initial session at the listed price; after that, the standard touch-up rate applies. Please follow the aftercare instructions provided and avoid sun exposure, makeup, and moisture on the brows for 10 days.

invoiceChecklist.item: Service performed and technique (e.g., microblading, powder brows, lamination)
invoiceChecklist.why: Clients often book several different services, and a clear label prevents confusion about what the price covers.

invoiceChecklist.item: Date of service and date of included touch-up
invoiceChecklist.why: Semi-permanent work involves a follow-up, and writing the date and window down avoids disputes over free versus paid touch-ups.

invoiceChecklist.item: Deposit paid and balance due
invoiceChecklist.why: Showing the deposit as a credit makes it clear how the final total was reached and protects your no-show or cancellation policy.

invoiceChecklist.item: Retail products sold, itemized separately
invoiceChecklist.why: Aftercare balms and tint kits are products, and in many states they are taxable while services are not, so keep them on their own lines.

invoiceChecklist.item: Package details and sessions remaining
invoiceChecklist.why: If a client prepays for a lamination series or touch-up bundle, noting sessions used and remaining prevents arguments later.

invoiceChecklist.item: Your license or permit number where required
invoiceChecklist.why: Many states require cosmetology, esthetician, or tattoo or body art licensing for semi-permanent work, and some clients and venues ask to see it. Check your local rules.

invoiceChecklist.item: Travel fee or event minimum for mobile jobs
invoiceChecklist.why: Travel time is real cost, and listing it as a line item shows the client what it is for.

brow-artist.paymentTerms: Brow services are usually paid at the time of appointment by card, cash, or a payment app, so invoices often serve as receipts. For microblading, powder brows, and bridal or group bookings, a deposit of $50 to $150 (or 25 to 50 percent for larger bookings) is common to hold the time slot and is typically non-refundable but transferable with notice. Many artists require 24 to 48 hours notice for cancellations and charge a fee or forfeit the deposit for late cancellations or no-shows. Events and bridal parties are usually paid in full before the date or at least half up front with the balance due on the day. If you send invoices for later payment, 7 days is a typical due date, with any late fee stated clearly in your booking policy.

tips.title: Take a deposit for every long appointment
tips.body: A semi-permanent session blocks two to three hours and uses single-use supplies. A deposit protects you from no-shows and late cancellations, and it should be collected at booking, not at the appointment.

tips.title: Define the touch-up window in writing
tips.body: State exactly how many weeks the included touch-up is valid and what happens after. Clients often assume it is free forever, and putting the window on the invoice and booking confirmation avoids awkward conversations.

tips.title: Separate services from retail
tips.body: Keep aftercare balms, tint kits, and brow products on their own invoice lines. This makes sales tax handling simpler if your state taxes products or certain services, so check what applies where you work.

tips.title: Charge for corrections and redos clearly
tips.body: If a client wants to fix work done elsewhere or needs a color correction, price it as a separate service with a consult, since it takes more time and carries more risk than a standard session.

tips.title: Track supplies and booth rent
tips.body: Pigments, needles, blades, numbing products, and booth or suite rent are your major costs. Review them yearly against your prices so your rates keep up with your real expenses.

faqs.question: Should I charge separately for the microblading touch-up?
faqs.answer: Most artists include one touch-up within a set window, commonly 4 to 8 weeks, either in the main price or at a reduced rate. List it as its own line on the invoice with the date or window so it is clear what is included and when it expires.

faqs.question: Do I charge sales tax on brow services?
faqs.answer: It depends on your state and sometimes your city. Many states do not tax personal services, but they usually tax retail products like balms and tint kits. Check with your state revenue department or a tax professional.

faqs.question: Is the deposit refundable?
faqs.answer: Most brow artists make deposits non-refundable but transferable if the client gives notice, often 24 to 48 hours. Whatever your policy is, put it in your booking confirmation and in the notes on your invoice.

faqs.question: How do I invoice a bridal party or group booking?
faqs.answer: List each person or service as a line item with the number of people and the per-person price, then add a travel fee and any early-start or minimum fee. Collect a deposit to hold the date and set the final payment due before the event.

faqs.question: Do I need to invoice if the client pays in person?
faqs.answer: It is still a good idea to give a receipt or paid invoice. It documents the service, any deposit and tip, and the touch-up window, and it gives you clean records for taxes.

estimate.intro: Brow artists give quotes mainly for semi-permanent work, bridal and event bookings, corrections of other artists' work, and packages. Clients usually compare price per session, whether a touch-up is included, the artist's experience and healing photos, and what the studio setting offers.

scopeChecklist.why: Microblading, powder brows, and combo brows differ in method, healing, and price, so the quote should say which one is planned.

scopeChecklist.item: Number of sessions and what the touch-up includes
scopeChecklist.why: Clients need to know whether the price covers just the first session or also a follow-up, and by when it must be done.

scopeChecklist.item: Patch test, consultation, and brow mapping
scopeChecklist.why: State whether these are included, since some artists charge a consultation fee that is credited to the service.
Fixing previous work can take extra sessions and may not be fully possible, so the quote should say what outcome is realistic.
Pregnancy, certain medications, skin conditions, and recent Botox or sun exposure may mean a delay or refusal, and the quote should say how that affects the booking.
Clients should know what is due to book and what happens if they reschedule or cancel.

scopeChecklist.item: Travel, setup, and party size for mobile or event jobs
scopeChecklist.why: Per-person pricing, minimums, and travel fees need to be set before the day to avoid disputes.

pricingTips.title: Quote by service, not by hour
pricingTips.body: Clients compare menu prices, so give a flat price for each service and explain what it covers. Hourly pricing is rarely used except for events or custom work.

pricingTips.title: Offer package options
pricingTips.body: Present a basic option and a bundled option, such as microblading with touch-up and aftercare, or a lamination series. Packages raise the average ticket and make comparison easier for the client.

pricingTips.title: Price correction work higher
pricingTips.body: Cover-ups and fixes of poor work take more time, planning, and sessions. Charge a consultation or a higher flat price, and state that results depend on the existing pigment and skin.

pricingTips.title: Show healing photos with the quote
pricingTips.body: Including a few healed examples that match the client's skin type and brow style helps justify your price and sets realistic expectations.

faqs.question: Should I charge for a consultation?
faqs.answer: Some artists offer free consultations for basic services and charge $25 to $75 for semi-permanent consults, credited toward the service if the client books. This filters out people who only want to compare prices.

faqs.question: How long should a quote be valid?
faqs.answer: Typically 30 days. Pigment, supplies, and your own pricing can change, and an expiration date lets you update your rates without honoring an old quote forever.

faqs.question: What if the client wants a different brow shape than I recommend?
faqs.answer: Document the agreed shape in the quote or consent form after mapping. If the client insists on a shape you think will not suit them, note it in writing so the expectation and the final result are clear.

business-coach.intro: Business coaches work with owners, founders, and managers on strategy, goals, accountability, and leadership. They invoice for one-on-one sessions, monthly coaching packages, group programs, workshops, and sometimes assessments or between-session support. Most are solo practitioners, so clear billing terms matter as much as the coaching itself.
business-coach.pricingModel: Most business coaches sell time in packages rather than single sessions. The common structure is a monthly retainer that includes a set number of sessions (often two to four 60-minute calls), plus limited email or messaging access between calls. Others sell a fixed-length engagement, such as a 3-month or 6-month program, billed in full upfront at a discount or in monthly installments. Hourly rates are used for one-off sessions, strategy intensives, and drop-in clients. Group coaching and masterminds are priced per seat, and workshops or team trainings are usually a flat day rate or per-attendee fee. Experience, niche, and client size drive price: coaching a solo founder costs less than coaching an executive team whose company is paying. Assessments, workbooks, and travel are typically billed separately or built into the package price.

rates.service: Monthly coaching retainer (2-4 sessions plus email support)
Strategy intensive (half day or full day)
Ad hoc advisory or email support outside package

items.description: Monthly business coaching retainer, March (4 x 60-min sessions, email support between calls)
Quarterly planning intensive, 3 hours (Q2 goals and revenue plan)
